result:
If I could change one thing, I’d make empathy structural: a built-in part of every law, market, institution, and decision, so that the impact on other people—especially those with the least power—would be as impossible to ignore as cost or profit.

Most cruelty and neglect survive because harm can be distant, diffuse, or denied. If that distance collapsed—if societies naturally had to reckon with who bears the cost of their choices—the world wouldn’t become perfect, but it would stop optimizing so easily for extraction, convenience, and power. It would tilt toward care.
